_doc: Everyday rules of tribe life: eating, storing food, births, the aurochs pens, burials, beds, and the folk life of children, art, mood and trade. Times are seconds unless named *_days. Read by sim.gd and folk.gd; see docs/CONFIG.md.

day._doc: The parts of the day, as [from, to] fractions of it (sim.day_frac(): 0 is midnight's other side of dawn; a part may wrap past 1.0, like [0.96, 0.12]). Read through sim.is_day_part(name) and sim.day_part(name). night: the rest hours (people sleep; orders given after night starts keep people up). dark: when the sky is dark (a little around the rest hours). dusk: golden light, people drift to the fire. dawn: pink light. morning: the first hours (waking talk, new calves). Meal times are in life.json.

gathering._doc: After hauling a load home, a gatherer goes back to the node they were working only if it is of a kind in `return_to` (a kill half butchered is not left to the crows); any other work is picked afresh from where they are, so the camp's gatherers spread over what is near home.

healing._doc: Getting well (sim.unit_needs). Wounds heal per second at `warm` near a fire (else `cold`) once fed above fed_above and unhurt for calm_secs; a yarrow poultice (herbs, within poultice_reach of the village, below poultice_below of full health) multiplies it by `poultice` for herb_secs. Willow-bark tea for the sick costs a herb every herb_secs. Fever hurts the sick by `fever` per second down to fever_floor of full health (to death when hungrier than fever_hungry or in winter). Cold hurts down to cold_floor unless it can kill; freezing_warn: the 'Freezing!' mark.

defense._doc: When a person is hit (sim.update_unit): within hit_secs of the blow they fight back, or flee below flee_below of full health (the belligerent never flee; children and scouts always do).

skills._doc: Skill levels (sim.gain_xp): the XP a level takes is xp_base + xp_per_lv x the level; levels stop at max_lv (past routine work they come in ranks earned by trials: config/ranks.json). tradition_xp: XP multipliers per skill while the tribe keeps a tradition. aura: the Centurion Aura, from someone holding combat rank aura.rank or higher: people within radius get their DEF times def_mult.

births._doc: Births (sim._update_births, sim.birth_rate()): one child per `every` seconds for every `per_lines` grown family lines (never slower than one per `every`), while there are beds free and the stores hold `min_food` (a count: a number or {base, per_pop}); each costs `cost` food and lifts the mood by `mood`. Past beds.crowd_at of the beds the rate tapers to nothing at full (beds.crowd_k), in winter it is `winter` times, and with the tribe's mood under `low_mood` it is `low_mood_mult` times.

fuel._doc: Winter fuel (sim.fuel_rate(), out_of_fuel()): in winter the fires burn per_head wood a second for each person (night_mult times in the dark); with no wood left the bonfires give no warmth until there is. The tribe's wood is its winter warmth.
fuel.alert: The woodpile is empty and the fires are dying: the tribe will freeze without wood!

strife._doc: Civil strife (life.gd): with at least min_pop people and the tribe's mood under `mood` for `days` days, the people rise and the chieftain must answer (dilemma 'strife'), at most every every_days days.

lod._doc: Level of detail (sim.hot(), the tick): people out of danger are updated every `every`-th tick with that many times the step, so a city of a thousand stays fast; anyone fighting, fleeing, reacting, in an emergency or hurt in the last hot_secs seconds is updated every tick.

tiers._doc: Settlement tiers (sim.tier_of(at), checked every `every` s for each of our settlements): the last row of `list` whose needs a settlement meets. Its people are those whose home is there; `pop`: at least this many; `beds`: at least this many beds; `built`: building types it must have (a list in the list: any one of them); `store`: the tribe's food storage at least; `era`: the age. A settlement rising to a tier other than the first is named (the next free name of `names`) and celebrated (an achievement, `feat`); `log` tells the chronicle (the place, the tier), `named` when it takes its name.
tiers.named: The people give their settlement a name: %s.

migration._doc: Families who come to live with the tribe (folk.add_family, the story action newcomers). Each day a family may move to us from an ally or a vassal (clan_chance) while we have free_beds and the clan keeps more than clan_keeps people. Wanderers: on a morning, with at least min_pop people, the mood at mood or better and free_beds beds free, with chance `chance`, count [min, max] wanderers ask to stay (dilemma 'wanderers'). Newcomers have skills up to skill_max and lift the mood by `mood`; at most most_at_once in one go.

beds._doc: Night rest (sim._night_rest): further than `far` from a bed, people camp where they are. Work given after night falls keeps people up, except the kinds in day_only, which wait for the morning whenever they were ordered (renovate: renovating and upgrading buildings). crowd_at: past this share of the beds taken the camp is crowded (sickness spreads more, births taper by crowd_k; a crowded settlement sends a family to one with a free bed and a fire of ours within fire_reach).

steward._doc: How the Steward picks work for each idle person, in this order: a building site near home (build_chance); crafts when there is food_per_head_art food a head and art_wood wood (art_chance); a want (see `wants`) once there is food_per_head food a head; wood when the stores are `full` (share of the cap); food below food_per_head a head; wood below low_wood; else the policy. Gatherers work within area_r of home. Work other than building and crafts is a stint of `shift` [min, max] seconds: then they come back idle (a gatherer hauls the load home first) and are given what is needed then; the chieftain's own orders have no shift. With wood_enough wood stacked (a count), wood work goes to food instead, or to the rites when the stores are full (unless the policy is wood). In autumn food comes before wood until the stores are autumn_fill full (the harvest rush). Food work goes first to a field or dock with a free place (structures.json `worked`) when fields_first is on.

vice._doc: The Vice-Chieftains. There are two offices (Steward, War Chief) and one slot at first; Tribal Code or the Council of Elders tradition opens the second. Every `every` seconds by day the Steward puts idle grown-ups within steward_reach of home to work. `wants`: what the tribe runs short of whatever the policy (except lore): while the store holds less than `below` of `res` and `when` holds (conditions as in scenario scripts), `share` of them go and gather it, if any can be gathered within want_reach of home (stone needs the tools; herbs and ore a known find). When beasts or raiders come within warchief_range of the village, the War Chief keeps `fighters` people on the nearest of them: the best fighters within `reach` of it, not sick and with at least min_hp of their health.

research._doc: A research contract that finishes a tech the tribe already knows turns the work into this (contract_system.gd _complete_research).

ward._doc: The totem ward, a chieftain's answer to beasts attacking a contract crew (contract_system.gd): what it costs and how far it scares them.

triggers._doc: When the built-in dilemmas come up (conditions as in scenario scripts).

mood.grumble: The people grumble and work without heart. A festival, art or a full belly would lift them.

improvements._doc: The village lays out improvements itself (improve.gd). planner: steward (only while a Steward is appointed) or anyone (the tribe's best at lore plans without one). Every `every` seconds by day, with fewer than `max_sites` of its sites unfinished (a count: a number or {base, per_pop}), the first entry of `list` that is wanted (`when`: conditions as in scenario scripts), known, affordable keeping `wood_reserve`, and has room within `reach` of the village (a count: it grows with the tribe) (near the structure type `near`) is laid out. If several are wanted, the Steward's LLM node may choose (`ask`; it waits `ask_wait` seconds, at most once per `ask_every`). A road entry ({"road": level id, "structure": "roadworks", "cells", "min_cells"}) makes the busiest trails near the village into that road.

list.reason: winter is coming, and the stores must keep.
the stores are nearly full and food would rot.
the stores could not hold what a winter eats.
the beds are nearly all taken: a large hut can become a longhouse.
the beds are nearly all taken: a hut can be made bigger.
the village has grown past its fires: people must keep warm.
an outpost has no fire to keep warm by.
the village is crowded: an outpost needs a home for those who will move there.
the beds are nearly all taken: the tribe needs room to grow.
a shrine brings lore and heals the sick.
the village has grown round its shrine: it wants a temple.
the most trodden trails can become a road.

buildings._doc: One building at a time (the building panel, and sim.renovate_one/upgrade/demolish for a game master). renovate_work: share of a building's work to rebuild it in the era's style (it costs half its wood, and stone_era3 stone from era 3). upgrades: what a built structure can become, in place; it costs the difference to the new one's wood and stone times upgrade_cost (at least min_wood), takes upgrade_work of the new one's work, needs its tech, and the building keeps working meanwhile. demolish: refund share of its wood and stone; never: kinds that can't be pulled down.

ring._doc: Walls (structures with "ring": the palisade) are laid out at a chosen radius, min-max in steps of step; their wood and work scale with it (the structure's own cost is for its own r).

contracts._doc: Task Contracts. settle_room: no new outpost while one of ours has this many beds or more to spare (contracts.settle_block()). titles: the name players read for a contract of each kind (plan_id is an internal id the leader picks, never shown); %s is the leader (settle), the wisdom sought (research), the enemy clan (war) or what is sought (seek). Read by contracts.title().
